title: Data manifest
description: The single contract between the Python pipeline (which writes web/public/data/manifest.json) and the web app (which reads it and nothing else about the data). Human explanation: docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md. Cross-field rules that JSON Schema cannot express are listed there and enforced by `python -m pipeline validate`.

schema.description: Contract version. Bump on any breaking change and update both sides in the same commit.

generated_at.description: UTC time the manifest was written, ISO 8601 with a trailing Z.

sites.description: One entry per place. May be empty before the first pipeline run.

slug.description: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. Used in file names and URLs.

date.description: Calendar date in UTC (YYYY-MM-DD) of the start of the acquisition. This matches granule names, the NASA catalog and NASA GIBS layer dates. It can differ from the local date at the site.

url.description: Resolved against the URL of manifest.json itself (so 'sample/hh_2008-10-12.tif' sits next to the manifest). Absolute https URLs are allowed for data hosted elsewhere.

release.description: Data maturity. 'sample' means a format-sample or simulated product that is NOT a NISAR observation.

bounds.description: [west, south, east, north] in degrees, EPSG:4326.

generator.description: Provenance of the processing, including whether its code was written with AI assistance.

git_commit.description: Short hash of the repository commit the pipeline ran from, when known. Ends in '+uncommitted' when the pipeline or contract code had uncommitted changes at the time.

summary.description: One or two plain sentences shown with the site.

is_sample.description: true when this site is NOT built from real NISAR observations. The app must then show `notice` prominently and permanently.

notice.description: Plain-language notice shown prominently with this site (required in practice when is_sample is true).

view.description: Optional initial map view. Without it the app fits `bounds`.

dates.description: Every acquisition the pipeline processed for this site, ascending by date. These are real acquisition dates, never a calendar.

missing_passes.description: Dates on which the 12-day repeat cycle predicts a pass that has no usable product. The app shows them as missing instead of hiding them.

stacks.description: Multi-band files for click queries: one band per date, so one range request returns a pixel's whole history.

stats.description: URL of this site's statistics file (contract/stats.schema.json).

overlays.description: Vector data from independent sources, drawn over the layers. Optional.

story.description: Steps of a guided tour of this site, in order. Optional.

extra.description: Escape hatch for experiments. Anything the app relies on must be promoted to a real field in this schema.

view.description: A map view: centre and zoom.

center.description: [longitude, latitude]. Latitude is limited to what a web map can show.

overlay.description: Vector data drawn on top of the raster layers, for example fire detections from another instrument. It is context from an independent source, never a NISAR measurement, and the app must show its credit wherever it is drawn.

kind.description: points: a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of Point features, coordinates [longitude, latitude] in EPSG:4326.

description.description: One plain sentence on how to read the overlay. Shown in the legend.

method.description: Short provenance: where the points come from and how they were selected. Details belong in docs/METHODS.md.

credit.description: Who to credit for this data.

date_property.description: Name of the feature property that holds the UTC calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) of each point. With it the app can show the points of a period instead of all of them.

date_range.description: First and last UTC date the overlay covers, inclusive. Outside this range the app must say that the overlay has no data, never that there were no points.

fields.description: Feature properties worth showing when a point is selected, in order.

count.description: Number of features in the file.

color.description: Drawing hint. Must stay readable on the layers it is drawn over and survive colour-blindness.

storyStep.description: One step of a guided tour: a short text and what the map should show while it is read. Everything a step points at must exist in the same site.

text.description: A few plain sentences. Interpretation is worded as a hypothesis.

layer.description: id of the layer to show.

date.description: For a per-date layer: the acquisition to show.

reference.description: For a pair layer: the earlier acquisition.

secondary.description: For a pair layer: the later acquisition.

overlays.description: ids of the overlays to switch on.

collection.description: Catalog short name(s) the granules came from.

release.description: 'mixed' only when dates come from more than one release; the app then says so wherever dates are compared.

stack.description: track_direction_frame. Only images of one stack may be compared directly.

frequency.description: Which radar band of the product the layers were read from.

posting_m.description: Pixel spacing of the source product in metres.

working_resolution_m.description: Pixel spacing after multilooking, before reprojection for display.

native_epsg.description: EPSG code of the source product grid.

granule.description: Granule name without the .h5 extension, exactly as in the catalog.

version.description: Processing version (CRID) from the granule name, e.g. P05023.

pols.description: Polarizations present in this granule for the frequency used. Read from the file, never assumed.

notes.description: Anything a reader should know about this date (partial frame, quality remark).

encoding.description: How the uint8 pixel values in a file map back to physical values. 0 is always nodata and is declared as nodata inside the file.

oneOf.description: physical = lo + (pixel - 1) * (hi - lo) / 254 for pixel in 1..255. Values outside [lo, hi] were clipped when the file was written.
Each pixel value is a class. Used for classified maps.

date.description: For kind 'per-date': the acquisition this file shows.

kind.description: per-date: one file per acquisition. pair: one file per (reference, secondary) pair of acquisitions, e.g. a change map. static: exactly one file for the whole site.

unit.description: Unit of the physical value, e.g. 'dB'. Empty string for unitless or categorical layers.

description.description: One plain sentence on how to read the layer. Shown in the legend.

method.description: Short provenance: how this layer was computed. Details belong in docs/METHODS.md.

display.description: Optional hint for drawing a linear-uint8 layer, in physical units. One fixed range for every date of a layer, so a difference between dates is a difference on the ground and not in the stretch.

min.description: Lower end of the drawn range. Must be less than max.

max.description: Upper end of the drawn range.

ramp.description: Name of a colour ramp the app knows. Must survive colour-blindness; never red against green.

diverging.description: true when the scale has a meaningful centre (for example 0 dB change).

layer.description: id of the per-date layer whose history this file holds.

band_dates.description: Band i (1-based) of the file is the acquisition band_dates[i-1]. Ascending.

resolution_m.description: Approximate ground pixel size of the stack, which may be coarser than the display layer.
